## M1 — Headless convergence

Two C++ CLI peers connect to an Erlang tracker (driving the C++ core through a Port) over WebSocket and replay the fuzzer's vectors, with connections dropped on purpose to exercise reconnect sync. Each peer authenticates by key and binds its client ID. There is no UI. This proves convergence over a patchy network, the BEAM-to-core boundary and the identity handshake before anyone draws anything.

## M2 — Inkscape plus no-JS

The Inkscape fork, running a C++ MUPPET, and a plain HTML browser served by a server-side MUPPET edit the same drawing. This is the first demo a person can see, and it tests the north star directly.

## M3 — Inkscape plus Wasm

A Wasm MUPPET in the browser joins as a full peer.

## M4 — Inkscape plus Conversations

Mobile and chat users take part through the XMPP bridge. What a stock Conversations user gets is [open question 7](/discussion/open-questions/#q7-what-does-a-conversations-user-get-in-m4).

## Where the gateway fits

The xtxp.link gateway and live web branching don't have a milestone yet. See [open question 9](/discussion/open-questions/#q9-where-does-the-web-gateway-sit-in-the-milestones). Folding it into M2 is a strong candidate, since the no-JS path of M2 *is* the gateway.
